account: Today I have kept morning office hours and attended the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill. The builder reports the west-bank routes passable, with no confirmed defects, hazards, or repair costs. No repairs are authorized; any future paid work needs an itemized price approved beforehand and payment after inspection. The secretary has no further correspondence and says freight is available today for ferry crossings and warehouse deliveries. At the mill I found 128 hay bales in the sale chest and left them untouched. This establishes stock on hand, but not quality, ownership beyond the sale stock, or delivery needs. The neighbour cannot answer those questions and now says freight is arriving and may help, though I have not yet seen freight myself. The unusual news is a repeated, vague rumour of a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Several townsfolk repeat the same phrase, and the neighbour has heard something similar, but none has supplied a clear proposal, source, or confirmed event. I do not know whether this concerns transport arrangements, building work, or merely a misunderstanding. The builder was asked to clarify the remark with the baker. For now I should not treat the rumour as town policy or a verified hazard. My remaining known appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters in the office at one, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at three, office at half past four, and home at seven.
